propositions: Production bugs result from store write paths that bypass canonical write seams using raw git commands, including in GitHub workflow YAML (e.g., bare git add/commit in cd .tickets-tracker context)

The canonical write surface has exactly two sanctioned seams: (1) store seam with locked write transactions and event appends that legitimately issue raw git internally, and (2) reconciler seam with git_adapter and _ref_lock update-ref operations

A deterministic two-layer CI lint must flag raw git mutation verbs (add/commit/rm/reset/update-ref/checkout/clean) in Python via AST analysis and in workflows/shell via cwd-aware context tracking, with fail-closed handling for opaque argv

Only sanctioned seams, store-maintenance commands, and disposable sandbox repositories may bypass the marker requirement; all other raw git mutations must carry an inline # raw-git-ok: <reason> marker with mandatory reason text

Module-agnostic flagging without dataflow analysis is feasible because rebar's Python writes git only for the tracker, its mirrors, or explicitly disposable sandbox repos, making every unmarked raw mutation either a seam internal, sandbox fixture, or bypass
